unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'the practical solution is to check the heating element assembly (which often includes the thermal cut-out or thermostat). If replacing these parts does not restore heat'

rationale: The opening step (check filter and vent hose, retest) was exactly right and the assistant correctly refused to name a part at first. It then undervalued the clogged-hose evidence, ranking the element above the thermal cut-out 'given the age', and never asked for the full model number or whether both heat settings were cold. When the customer said they had no multimeter, the correct move was to refer to an engineer; instead it effectively endorsed blind replacement of the heater assembly, mentioning an engineer only as a fallback for the control board. No unsafe instructions or invented facts, but the homeowner is left to order parts untested and without a confirmed model.
